PP2 · Chapter 7 of 7

Days, months and clocks

Talk about daily routines, weekday order and whole hours together.

  1. See it
  2. Try it
  3. Practise it
  4. Print it
  5. Check it

This chapter works best after Follow the picture clues. You can still look around, or jump to the check.

By the end I can…

  • I can say the day before or after.
  • I can put familiar months in order.
  • I can recognise a whole hour on a clock.

1 See it

Screen 1 of 4

Day and night

The sun is out in the day.

The moon is out at night.

Each day has a day time and a night time.

Screen 2 of 4

Seven days make a week

Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday.

Friday, Saturday, Sunday.

After Sunday a new week starts.

Screen 3 of 4

Twelve months make a year

There are 12 months in a year.

January is first. December is last.

After March comes April.

Screen 4 of 4

Whole hours

The short hand points to 3.

The long hand points to 12.

It is 3 o'clock.

Words to know
week
7 days. Monday to Sunday, then it starts again.
month
There are 12 months in a year.
o'clock
The long hand points up to 12. The short hand shows the hour.

For parents

What your child learns

Your child talks about day and night, puts days and months in order, and reads a whole hour on a clock. Practise and Check use the Class 1 time questions at level 1, so sit alongside your child.

A common slip

Mixing up the order of months or days. Sing the days in order. Use a wall calendar and tick off each day.

5-minute home activity: Daily routine clock

  1. At breakfast, say "It is 7 o'clock" and show the clock.
  2. Ask, "What day is it? What day comes next?"
  3. Point to today on a wall calendar.
  4. Match one routine to an hour, like bedtime at 8 o'clock.
